title: Arithmetic in Python
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Number workshop
objectives: know which arithmetic operator to use for each kind of calculation
understand the difference between /, // and % and what each one hands back
know how to round a result and how to draw a random number
starter: Work these out by hand, with no computer: 17 / 5, 17 // 5, 17 % 5 and 2 ** 5. Beside each answer write whether Python gives a whole number or a decimal.

stations.name: The four operations
stations.fact: The * was chosen for multiply because early keyboards had no times sign on them.
stations.challenge: Which operator would you use to halve the price of a pencil?

Ask the user for three whole numbers. Add all three together and display [total] and nothing else.
Ask the user for three whole numbers. Add the first two together, multiply that answer by the third, and display [answer] and nothing else.

stations.name: Whole number division
stations.fact: % is the quickest test for an even number: n % 2 is 0 whenever n is even.
stations.challenge: How many full crates of 12 do 50 returned books fill, and how many are left over?

stations.name: Powers and roots
stations.fact: ** is the exponent operator, and exponent is simply another word for power.

stations.name: Rounding
stations.fact: Python rounds a value ending in exactly .5 towards the even number, so round(2.5) is 2.
stations.challenge: Why does a till round to 2 decimal places rather than to a whole number?

stations.name: Random numbers
stations.fact: A computer works its random numbers out with a formula, so they are really pseudo-random.
stations.challenge: Why would a program ever want its random numbers to be predictable?

final.title: Final challenge: pick the operator
final.instr: write your answer for each one.
rows: How many full boxes of 10
How many are left over

Whole minutes in 200 seconds
The seconds left after those minutes
The area of a square

keyq: How do you choose between /, // and % when the answer to a calculation has to come out as a whole number?
exam: A program works out how many full boxes of 6 eggs a crate will fill, and the line reads boxes = eggs / 6. State what is wrong with the result this gives, and write the line corrected.
Write a program that reads a number of minutes and prints it as a number of whole hours and the minutes left over.
Write a program that reads two amounts of money in pounds and prints their mean, rounded to two decimal places.
confidence: Rounding a result and drawing a random number
